common_name: Essence of Royalty Daylily (Lavender Purple Rebloomer)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Essence of Royalty bears lavender-purple flowers with a deeper eye above a green throat on well-branched scapes.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Bred by Jack Carpenter and registered in 2002, Essence of Royalty is a tetraploid bearing lavender-purple flowers about six inches across with a deeper purple eye above a green throat, held on scapes roughly 26 inches tall. It opens its main flush in midseason and reblooms later, and has been used as a parent in several later Carpenter hybrids, including 'Warrior Victorious'. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Texas Blue Eyes Daylily (Lavender with Blue Eyezone)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun; Texas Blue Eyes bears soft lavender flowers patterned with a lavender-blue eyezone above a green throat.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in fertile, well-drained soil in full sun. Bred by Jack Carpenter and registered in 2004, Texas Blue Eyes is an evergreen tetraploid bearing soft lavender flowers about 5.5 inches across patterned with a lavender-blue eyezone above a green throat, held on scapes around 20 inches tall. It opens an early-to-midseason flush and reblooms reliably through summer, and has been used as a parent in several later Carpenter hybrids, including 'Warrior Victorious'. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Banana Pepper Spider Daylily (Deep Yellow Spider)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Banana Pepper Spider is a narrow-petaled spider daylily bred from 'Green Widow' and 'Kindly Light'.

directions: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Bred by H. Herrington from a cross of 'Green Widow' and 'Kindly Light' and registered in 1994, Banana Pepper Spider is a semi-evergreen diploid spider daylily bearing deep yellow self flowers about eight inches across with a vivid green throat, held on scapes around 44 inches tall. It opens an early-to-midseason flush with reliable rebloom, and won the American Hemerocallis Society's Harris Olson Spider Award in 2017. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to keep bloom counts high.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Carminea forms a small, arching mound smothered in starry pink flowers in late spring.

directions: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in average, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Introduced around 1900 as a hybrid of Deutzia gracilis and Deutzia purpurascens, Carminea is a compact, rounded shrub to about 3 feet with gracefully arching branches and dark green foliage. In late spring it bears large panicles of small, star-shaped flowers, pale rosy pink within and flushed deeper rose-carmine on the reverse and in bud, giving a two-toned effect across the bush; it was later used as a parent of the U.S. National Arboretum introduction 'Nikko Blush'. Like other deutzia it blooms on the previous year's wood, so prune lightly right after flowering to maintain shape without sacrificing next year's display.
